title: Depth-Optimal Quantum Compilation
abstract: We achieve the first constant-depth circuit for arbitrary single-qubit gate synthesis. Unlike prior approaches, the construction is fully unitary and requires no pre-supplied catalyst. For any constant $δ>0$, it $\varepsilon$-approximates an arbitrary single-qubit gate using $O(\log^{1+δ}(1/\varepsilon))$ clean ancillae, Hadamard and $T$ single-qubit gates, $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$-width generalized Toffoli gates, and sublogarithmic-width Fan-Out gates. We further eliminate Fan-Out entirely, showing that Hadamard, $T$, and generalized Toffoli gates alone suffice for constant-depth synthesis. When restricted to the standard bounded-width gate model, our construction has depth $O(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$, and we prove a matching $Ω(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$-depth lower bound. Overall, we establish that $Θ(\log\log(1/\varepsilon))$-depth is unavoidable with only bounded-width gates, yet allowing even logarithmic-width multi-qubit gates suffices to achieve constant-depth synthesis.   These results also reveal new structure in shallow quantum circuit complexity. We give a depth-preserving real simulation of bounded-error decision computation, showing that every depth-$d$ QAC circuit can be simulated in depth $O(d)$ using only Hadamard, $X$, and generalized Toffoli gates. Thus arbitrary single-qubit rotations and complex amplitudes do not increase the bounded-error decision power of QAC, even at constant depth. In particular, this reduces the long-standing conjecture Parity$\notin$QAC$^0$ to proving a Parity lower bound against circuits consisting only of Hadamard, $X$, and generalized Toffoli gates. More generally, this real normal form exposes a direct correspondence between the standard shallow-depth quantum circuit hierarchy and a hierarchy of Forrelation circuits with restricted oracle families.
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of quantum circuit complexity, achieving constant-depth synthesis for single-qubit gates using restricted gate sets. It establishes that while bounded-width gates impose a logarithmic depth overhead, allowing wider gates collapses the depth to a constant. The research also deeply connects quantum circuit power to algebraic structures via Forrelation quantities.
main_problem: The paper addresses determining the minimum circuit depth required to synthesize arbitrary quantum gates and characterizing the computational power of quantum circuits under various gate restrictions.
main_result: Constant-depth synthesis for single-qubit gates is achievable using only Hadamard, T, and generalized Toffoli gates, provided multi-qubit gates have sufficient width. Furthermore, it establishes deep connections between standard quantum circuit models and structured Fourier representations.
method: The authors use techniques involving depth-optimal compilation, establishing lower bounds that match upper bounds, and employing structured Fourier analysis to prove equivalences between different quantum circuit models.
model_or_system: The model is quantum computation realized through quantum circuits, focusing on decision problems (QAC) and the synthesis of single-qubit gates using specific universal gate sets.
key_observables: Circuit Depth, Acceptance Probability ($p_C(x)$), Forrelation quantity ($\Phi_m(g_x)$), and Ancilla Count.
important_parameters: Approximation precision ($\epsilon$), Circuit Depth ($D(n)$), and Gate Width (bounded vs. unbounded).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on the ability to perform partial-to-full Hadamard conversions and assumes bounded-error computation for the final characterizations.
figures_summary: No specific figure summaries are available, but the notes reference tables summarizing the standard, universal, and real circuit hierarchies.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first tackling gate synthesis depth, then analyzing the depth-preserving real simulation of decision computation, and finally establishing deep structural equivalences between quantum circuit classes using Fourier representations and Forrelation quantities.
why_interesting: The work provides rigorous complexity bounds for shallow quantum circuits, which is crucial for understanding the feasibility of near-term quantum computation architectures and for developing lower bounds for quantum supremacy demonstrations.
